supported_claims.text: 忘 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 心 contributes the meaning category “heart/mind,” and 亡 supplies a sound cue. The analysis is recorded in the Han lexicographic tradition and in summaries of bronze and later forms.
The supplied seal-script illustration represents the received 心-and-亡 analysis, but is a modern redraw rather than an ancient artifact image.

A cited Baxter–Sagart comparison gives 亡 *maŋ and 忘 *maŋ / *maŋ-s; the entries also give Middle Chinese 亡 mjang and 忘 mjang / mjangH. This supports a sound comparison in that reconstruction system, without dating the compound.
The historical lexicographic gloss is 不識也, “not to recognize/know.” Current reference material glosses 忘 as “forget; neglect; miss, omit.”

limitations.text: The evidence supports 心 as a semantic component and 亡 as phonetic; it does not establish a separate pictorial origin for either component within 忘 or show that 忘 depicts a scene.
No securely dated oracle-bone example or Shang-era attestation was verified. Listed bronze and later forms do not establish the graph’s earliest occurrence.

No dated early textual uses or ordered development among “forget,” “neglect,” “miss,” and “omit” were established. The historical gloss and current dictionary glosses do not by themselves establish that chronology.
The proposed account that 忘 arose from 亡 with a perfective suffix is unverified in this research; the evidence does not establish that word-history account or a whole-graph loan.

The current Mandarin pair is 亡 wáng and 忘 wàng, but current readings do not establish the ancient sound relation. The dossier’s same-system historical comparison supports a comparison, while not proving a particular sound change or the date of formation.
